title: How do you find a missing movement in a mine lift?
description: Seven mine lift sentences each have a missing number. Picturing the shaft shows how far the lift moves, up or down, to fill every blank, and each answer is checked by adding it back.
teaching_notes: One idea: the missing movement is the target level take away the starting level, found by counting through the ground. Watch for students who write the target level itself as the movement.

video_script.why: The child fills seven missing numbers by picturing the mine shaft and counting the climb or drop from the starting level to the target level.
video_script.substitution: The seven sentences of the book question, solved in three groups, with a check by adding the movement back.
video_script.anchor: a lift in a mine, with levels measured in metres from the ground
video_script.payoff_line: The missing number is the target level take away the starting level.

final_answer.spoken: positive one hundred sixty, negative two hundred forty, positive two hundred fifty, negative one hundred fifty, negative one hundred sixty, positive one hundred sixty and negative two hundred forty

maths_rules: starting level + movement = target level, so movement = target level - starting level
ground demo: from +30 up to +100 is 70 m up, so (+30) + (+70) = +100
g. (-200) - (+40): from +40 down to 0 is 40 m, then 200 m more, 240 m down, so -240
video_script.design: One shaft with the ground marked, three groups of sentences, and a check line that adds the movement to the starting level.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a mine lift in a shaft with the ground marked 0 m; the sentence (+40) + ___ = +200

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the mine shaft is drawn with the ground marked 0 m
marks.ask: seven sentences with blanks slide in as a list
marks.look: the lift stops at +40 m and the level +200 m lights up

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about a lift in a mine.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Seven sentences are given, and each one has a missing number.
<bookmark mark='look'/>In the first one, the lift is at positive forty metres and must reach positive two hundred.
Which way does it go, and how far?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: (+30) + ___ = +100; the lift rises from +30 m to +100 m with 70 m counted; Target level - Starting level = Movement

marks.demo: the lift rises from +30 m to +100 m and 70 m is counted
marks.rule: the line Target level - Starting level = Movement is written

narration: <bookmark mark='demo'/>A lift at positive thirty metres must reach positive one hundred. It rises seventy metres, so the blank is positive seventy.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The blank is the movement, which is the target level take away the starting level.

marks.given: the seven sentences are written in a list

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four sentences with a blank, and three take aways.

beats.on_screen: To find: the missing number in each

marks.find: the words missing number are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the missing number in each one.

marks.one: the first group is marked: the lift stays on one side of the ground
marks.a: an arrow rises from +40 m to +200 m and 160 up is written
marks.d: an arrow falls from -50 m to -200 m and 150 down is written

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, the lift stays on one side of the ground.
<bookmark mark='a'/>From positive forty up to positive two hundred is one hundred sixty metres up.
<bookmark mark='d'/>From negative fifty down to negative two hundred is one hundred fifty metres down.

marks.two: the second group is marked: the lift crosses the ground
marks.b: an arrow falls from +40 m to the ground and then to -200 m, and 240 down is written
marks.c: an arrow rises from -50 m to the ground and then to +200 m, and 250 up is written

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, the lift crosses the ground.
<bookmark mark='b'/>From positive forty down to the ground is forty, and two hundred more, so two hundred forty down.
<bookmark mark='c'/>From negative fifty up to the ground is fifty, and two hundred more, so two hundred fifty up.

marks.three: the third group is marked: the take aways, target level first
marks.e: an arrow falls from -40 m to -200 m and 160 down is written
marks.f: an arrow rises from +40 m to +200 m and 160 up is written
marks.g: an arrow falls from +40 m to the ground and then to -200 m, and 240 down is written

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, the take aways, with the target level first.
<bookmark mark='e'/>Negative two hundred take away negative forty. The lift drops from negative forty to negative two hundred, one hundred sixty down.
<bookmark mark='f'/>Positive two hundred take away positive forty. The lift climbs one hundred sixty.
<bookmark mark='g'/>Negative two hundred take away positive forty. It drops forty to the ground and two hundred more, two hundred forty down.

beats.on_screen: Check: starting level + movement = target level;  (+40) + (-240) = -200;  (-50) + (+250) = +200

marks.check: the check line starting level plus movement equals target level is written

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check by adding the movement back to the starting level.
<bookmark mark='down'/>Positive forty plus negative two hundred forty lands on negative two hundred.
<bookmark mark='up'/>Negative fifty plus positive two hundred fifty lands on positive two hundred.

marks.rule: the line target level take away starting level glows
marks.blanks: the four filled blanks are boxed
marks.takes: the three take aways are boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>The missing number is the target level take away the starting level.
<bookmark mark='blanks'/>The first two blanks are positive one hundred sixty and negative two hundred forty.
The next two are positive two hundred fifty and negative one hundred fifty.
<bookmark mark='takes'/>The three take aways are negative one hundred sixty, positive one hundred sixty and negative two hundred forty.
